package_opens.note: The mayor of Hazevale is handed the king's package and opens it; the fire in it burns the village. Played when the delivery quest completes (the campaign's cutscene node).

beats.text: The mayor of Hazevale turns the package over in his hands, and breaks the red wax with his thumbnail, the way a host does with a gift.
Inside, nested in straw, lies a ring of red stones. The stones are glowing.
[[YELLOW]]The mayor of Hazevale speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"It is warm. Why is it so warm..."[[/]]
[[RED]]Fire pours out of the box. It does not burn in one place. It swirls, and dances, and climbs the air like something let off its leash.[[/]]
It runs around the rim of the square, over the well and down the lane, a bright wheel of flame, and wherever it passes the thatch goes up like paper.
[[RED]]The mayor of Hazevale cries out once, and then there is no mayor.[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa shouts:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Out! Get out of the square!"[[/]]
You run, and the fire runs with you: smoke, the roar of it, a roof falling in somewhere behind. Then it is simply over, as if a hand had closed on it.
When you stop, there is nothing left of Hazevale but black timbers, and ash drifting down like snow.
The wind drops. In the quiet, thin and far off to the south, someone is crying.

kessa_deduces.note: After Ryn has told what happened to her mother: Kessa works out what the king meant by the package, and the argument that follows. Ends with Kessa given way.

beats.text: Captain Kessa has gone very still beside you.
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"A summoner's child, and the fog was her mother's. Do you see it now, Captain? It was never a gift, and it was never about the ring."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"The king needed Hazevale gone. Every roof and every soul in it. A village that keeps a dragon asleep is a village he could not leave standing."[[/]]
She looks at the girl, and her hand finds the haft of her spear.
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Every soul. That means her. If we go back to Varenholt with a witness still breathing, we are the ones who answer for it."[[/]]
You step between Kessa and the child. [[BLUE]]"No."[[/]] It comes out harder than you meant it to.
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"She saw it, Captain. She will tell it to the first person who asks."[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"She is a girl,"[[/]] you say. [[BLUE]]"We have done enough for one king today. I will not do this too."[[/]]
For a long moment the only sounds are the girl's crying and the ash settling. Kessa's jaw works. Then the spear point sinks to the ground.
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Then he can send his own blade for her. I am done with this. What do we do?"[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"We take her, and we do not go back to Varenholt,"[[/]] you say.

[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Deserters, then. Well. It is a better thing to be than what we were this morning."[[/]] She turns to the child, and her voice changes. [[GREEN]]"Easy, little one. Easy."[[/]]

colossus_quake.note: Ryn will not come, and calls the colossus; the quake brings the mountain down. Then the party wakes in a wood far from Hazevale, Kessa gone (taken out of the world; the next scene says so) and Ryn unconscious in the player's arms.

beats.text: Ryn's crying stops. It stops all at once, and that is worse.
[[YELLOW]]Ryn speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Mother said, when the people with the red ring come, do not run. Sing."[[/]]
She sings: three notes, low, and the ground answers every one. The ash on the ground begins to dance.
[[RED]]A Colossus rises out of the earth behind her, vast and grey, and the sky is a smaller thing than it was.[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Captain Kessa shouts:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Ryn, no! Ryn, stop!"[[/]]
[[RED]]The Colossus lifts one hand and brings it down. A Quake rolls out from the shrine, across the ruins and the valley, and the whole world shudders.[[/]]
High above, the mountainside lets go. The sight comes first, and then the sound, and the sound is the end of everything.
You reach for the girl. You reach for Kessa. Then there is only stone, and dark.
[[CYAN]]A long time passes.[[/]]

wake_in_the_wood.note: Played on waking in Thornwood after the quake: Kessa is gone, and the girl is unconscious in the player's arms.

beats.text: You wake on your back in dead leaves, with the taste of dust in your mouth. Pale morning light comes down through a roof of branches.
Your arms ache. They are wrapped around something small and limp: the girl, Ryn, breathing slowly, deep in a sleep that is not sleep. You must have held on to her the whole way down.
There is no sign of Kessa. You call her name until your voice is a rasp, and the wood gives nothing back.
Through the trees to the east the ground rises into pale dunes, and a thin road runs toward a smudge of roofs hazy with heat. You settle the girl against your shoulder, and begin to walk. (go east)

reach_the_inn.note: The end of the slice: the player carries Ryn into the inn of the desert village.

beats.text: The innkeeper looks up as you come in, takes one look at the child in your arms, and is already moving.
[[YELLOW]]The innkeeper speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Gods. Here, there is a bed in the back room. Lay her down. I will send for the healer's wife."[[/]]
You lay Ryn on a clean pallet, and she turns her face to the wall without waking. Outside, a hot wind rattles the shutters.
[[CYAN]]For the first time since Ilmara, there is nowhere you are being sent.[[/]]
